title: Graph ordering can place children before parents when timestamps tie or skew

evidence.quote:
const ordered = commits
      .filter((c) => laneByBranch.has(c.branchId))
      .slice()
      .sort((a, b) => (a.createdAt < b.createdAt ? -1 : a.createdAt > b.createdAt ? 1 : 0));

const ordered = commits
      .filter((c) => offsetByBranch.has(c.branchId))
      .slice()
      .sort((a, b) => (a.createdAt < b.createdAt ? -1 : a.createdAt > b.createdAt ? 1 : 0));

reasoning: Both graph components derive vertical or horizontal position solely from createdAt order, then draw edges by parentId. If a child and parent share the same timestamp, arrive in child-first prop order, or have clock-skewed timestamps, the child is positioned before the parent and the version tree contradicts ancestry. A version graph should remain topological even when timestamps are non-unique.
reproduction: Pass two commits with the same createdAt where the second is the parent of the first and the child appears first in the commits array; BranchGraph renders the child above the parent and HorizontalBranchGraph draws the edge backward in time.
recommendation: Order commits topologically by parentId within the visible set, using createdAt and a stable id/index only as tie-breakers where ancestry does not constrain order.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the package test script is a no-op, so there is no graph ordering regression coverage.
suggestedRegressionTest: Render both graph components with parent/child commits sharing createdAt in child-first input order and assert the parent is positioned before the child.
minimumFixScope: Add a shared ancestry-aware commit ordering helper and use it in both BranchGraph and HorizontalBranchGraph.
